Judge candidates with a model, in more than one order

Source: R/core-bench-judge.R
hr_judge.Rd

Asks a model to choose between candidates ("select"), to compare two ("pairwise") or to grade one against a reference ("grade"), once per presentation order, and combines the verdicts. The candidates are shown under the letters A, B, ... only; their names, and so their source, are not sent. With orders = 2 the order is swapped on the second request (see hr_judge_config()); when the verdicts, mapped back to the candidates they name, differ between orders, the result is "unresolved" with degradation = "judge_inconsistent", never a pick. Position bias of this kind is common in model judges (Zheng et al. 2023; Wang et al. 2024).

Usage

hr_judge(
  candidates,
  client,
  mode = c("select", "grade", "pairwise"),
  reference = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  orders = 2,
  rubric,
  schema = NULL,
  trace = NULL,
  governor = NULL,
  draw_index = 0L
)

# S3 method for class 'hr_judgement'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

candidates

The candidates, a character vector (or a list of single strings). Names, when every candidate has a distinct one, identify them in value; otherwise their positions do. "select" takes 2 to 26, "pairwise" exactly 2 and "grade" exactly 1.

client

A gr_client.

mode

"select", "grade" or "pairwise".

reference

Text the judge sees beside the candidates: evidence or a reference answer. Required for "grade".

model

The judge's model; the client's model when NULL.

orders

Presentation orders. See hr_judge_config().

rubric

What the judge decides, in words.

schema

NULL, or a reply schema with a string verdict property.

trace

Optional gr_trace of the run being judged.

governor

Optional hr_governor() for the judge's requests.

draw_index

Draw index passed to every request (see gr_call()).

x

An hr_judgement.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class hr_judgement, a list with

value

The verdict: the chosen candidate's name (or position) for "select", that or "tie" for "pairwise", the grade for "grade"; NA unless outcome is "answered".

outcome

"answered", "unresolved" or "failed".

verdicts

A data frame with one row per order: order, shown (the candidates in the order shown, or "reference,response"), label, ok, verdict (as the judge gave it), value (mapped back to a candidate), reason and error.

degradation

"judge_inconsistent" when unresolved, else NA.

swap_checked

FALSE when only one order was asked.

judge_cost

A list of usd (NA when the model has no price), tokens_in, tokens_out and calls, over the judge's own requests.

mode, model, candidates (the ids), config_hash

What was judged and under which configuration.

trace

The judge's own gr_trace.

Details

Every request goes through gr_call()'s path, so the governor checks it before it is sent, a gr_cache() keys it with draw_index, and the trace records it, under the label judge.<mode>.o<k> for order k. The requests are recorded in a trace of the judge's own ($trace), never in trace, and their cost is reported in $judge_cost, so a run's cost never includes the judging of it. When trace is given, the judge is held to what that run's governor has left (calls, dollars and tokens) and a local note naming the judge's trace and cost is added to it. governor, if given, is used instead.

A failed request, or a reply with no allowed verdict, makes the result "failed".

References

Wang, P., Li, L., Chen, L., Cai, Z., Zhu, D., Lin, B., Cao, Y., Kong, L., Liu, Q., Liu, T. and Sui, Z. (2024). Large language models are not fair evaluators. Proceedings of ACL 2024, 9440-9450.

Zheng, L., Chiang, W.-L., Sheng, Y., Zhuang, S., Wu, Z., Zhuang, Y., Lin, Z., Li, Z., Li, D., Xing, E. P., Zhang, H., Gonzalez, J. E. and Stoica, I. (2023). Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36.

See also

hr_judge_config(), hr_judge_validate(), hr_scorer_judge()

Other judges: hr_judge_config(), hr_judge_ppi(), hr_judge_validate(), hr_scorer_judge()

Examples

# A judge that always picks the candidate naming Paris.
fair <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
  txt <- messages[[2]]$content
  pick <- if (grepl("Candidate A:\nParis", txt, fixed = TRUE)) "A" else "B"
  sprintf('{"verdict": "%s", "reason": "It names the capital."}', pick)
})
j <- hr_judge(c(first = "Paris", second = "Lyon"), fair, mode = "select",
              rubric = "Which candidate names the capital of France?")
j$value
#> [1] "first"
j$verdicts[, c("order", "shown", "verdict", "value")]
#>   order        shown verdict value
#> 1     1 first,second       A first
#> 2     2 second,first       B first

# A judge that always says "A" follows the position, so it is unresolved.
first <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) '{"verdict": "A", "reason": "."}')
hr_judge(c("Paris", "Lyon"), first, mode = "select",
         rubric = "Which candidate names the capital of France?")$outcome
#> [1] "unresolved"
